rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the overlapping early cluster responds to slope. This should spread slope-sensitive pairs while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Probe a substantial temperature shift at the original slope to change selectivity within the early overlapping cluster. Higher temperature should also preserve ample time margin for subsequent gradient refinement.

The temperature increase nearly resolved the mixture and left substantial time margin. Lengthening the gradient at 60 C tests whether the remaining critical pair can reach R ≥ 1.5 while the last peak stays below 10 minutes.

The remaining pair at 60 C worsened with a shallower gradient, suggesting selectivity rather than gradient duration is limiting. Test the opposite temperature endpoint for a more favorable elution order while retaining the broad, fast gradient.

Return to the favorable high temperature and shift the starting organic fraction to probe selectivity in the remaining critical pair. The first peak previously eluted at 1.30 minutes, leaving some room to raise phi0 without making it unretained.

Injection 6 reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method, checking whether the two closest early pairs remain above R = 1.5.

Lowering phi1 slightly makes the eight-minute gradient shallower, targeting recovery of the small resolution deficits without returning to a ten-minute gradient. The last peak previously eluted near phi = 0.64, so phi1 = 0.85 retains ample elution strength.

Keep the successful gradient slope from injection 8 but shift the organic window upward to shorten retention. This tests whether improved selectivity in the last critical pair can offset compression of the earlier peaks.
Test a five-degree temperature adjustment at the faster shifted window to measure its effect on the single unresolved pair. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Return to the favorable starting composition and temperature, with a narrower window and six-minute gradient. Its slope lies between the successful injection 8 and nearly resolved injection 7, testing a faster boundary while keeping phi1 above the observed last-peak elution fraction.

Injection 11 still has a subthreshold pair despite its rounded CRF of 1.000. Test whether a shallower gradient restores the early-pair resolution lost at phi0 = 0.20, while the narrower organic window keeps retention within the scoring time limit.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 11 to bring its R = 1.49 pair above threshold. This slightly shallower six-minute gradient should preserve full resolution with a last-peak time close to the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

The maximum CRF is already secured, but the fastest methods have little resolution margin. Test a modestly shallower gradient at the successful starting composition to improve the critical-pair margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test the unexamined starting fraction between 0.05 and 0.15 with a faster gradient. Lowering phi0 may improve the earlier critical pair, while the steeper slope may help the later pair that worsened with shallower gradients at low phi0.

Test whether further shallowing at the favorable starting composition increases the minimum resolution while retaining maximum CRF. Extrapolation from injections 6 and 14 places the last peak near 9 minutes, below the time-penalty threshold.

Refine the speed boundary between injection 8, which fully resolved every pair, and injection 7, which narrowly failed. This intermediate endpoint tests whether the last peak can elute sooner than 6.04 minutes without sacrificing maximum CRF.

Test whether a shallower gradient can compensate for the selectivity loss at 55 C and provide a fully resolved lower-temperature alternative. The stronger endpoint and moderate slope should keep all compounds eluting below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Refine around injection 8, the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, by lowering the endpoint one step. This should provide slightly more resolution margin while keeping the last peak near 6.3 minutes and preserving maximum CRF.

Injection 18 narrowly missed full resolution at 55 C; lengthen its gradient one step to recover the remaining pair. The projected last-peak time remains below 10 minutes, making this a plausible maximum-score alternative at lower temperature.

Test a slope between injections 6 and 14 to obtain more resolution margin than the fastest method without extending retention as far as injection 14. The neighboring results support full resolution with the last peak around 7 minutes, preserving maximum CRF.

Refine around the fully resolved higher-starting-organic method from injection 12 using a slightly shallower slope and a stronger endpoint. This should preserve maximum CRF while adding a little margin to its limiting early pair.

Test the intermediate slope between injections 6 and 21, both of which achieved maximum CRF. This should retain full resolution with modestly more critical-pair margin than injection 6 and a shorter retention time than injection 21.

Trim the endpoint of injection 13 by one step to improve critical-pair resolution while retaining a six-minute programmed gradient. The last peak may enter the final hold, but neighboring runs suggest it should still elute comfortably before the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Use the final injection to test a shorter programmed gradient with nearly the same favorable slope as injection 21, targeting full resolution with useful margin and a last peak near 7.2 minutes.
